name: Intramuros
blurb: The 400-year-old walled city — cobblestone streets, Fort Santiago, and San Agustin Church.

name: Rizal Park (Luneta)
blurb: Manila's grand central park with the Rizal Monument, gardens, and bay sunset views.

name: National Museum of Fine Arts
blurb: Home to the Spoliarium and centuries of Filipino art inside a neoclassical landmark.

name: Manila Cathedral
blurb: The country's premier basilica — a Romanesque beauty at Plaza Roma, rebuilt after WWII.

name: Binondo
blurb: The world's oldest Chinatown — come hungry for dumplings, hopia, and street-food crawls.

name: Bamboo Bike Tour of Intramuros
blurb: Guided bamboo-bike ride through Intramuros with stops at hidden courtyards and cafés.

name: Manila Bay Sunset Cruise
blurb: Sail past the skyline as the famous Manila Bay sunset paints the water gold.

name: Divisoria Bargain Hunt
blurb: The ultimate budget shopping maze — clothes, souvenirs, and snacks at wholesale prices.

name: Poblacion Nightlife
blurb: Rooftop bars and late-night eats in Makati's trendiest block.

name: Manam (Greenbelt)
blurb: Modern Filipino comfort food — the crispy sisig and watermelon sinigang are must-orders.

name: Seaside Dampa
blurb: Pick your seafood fresh from the market and have it cooked your way, dampa-style.

name: Aristocrat Restaurant
blurb: A 1936 Manila institution famous for chicken barbecue and java rice by the bay.

name: Yardstick Coffee
blurb: Third-wave coffee in a minimalist space — a favorite of Manila's creative crowd.

name: Burnham Park
blurb: Baguio's green heart — rent a swan boat on the lagoon or bike around the park.

name: Mines View Park
blurb: Classic lookout over the old mining town with souvenir stalls and photo ops.

name: Camp John Hay
blurb: Pine forests, picnic groves, and the Tree Top Adventure rope courses.

name: Session Road
blurb: Baguio's main drag — restaurants, cafés, and people-watching day and night.

name: BenCab Museum
blurb: National Artist BenCab's hilltop museum of Cordillera art with a farm café.

name: Strawberry Picking in La Trinidad
blurb: Pick your own strawberries at the La Trinidad farm, 30 minutes from the city.

name: Tree Top Adventure
blurb: Ziplines and hanging bridges through the Camp John Hay pine canopy.

name: Baguio Night Market
blurb: Hunt for ukay-ukay thrift finds and street food along Harrison Road after dark.

name: Tam-awan Village
blurb: Reconstructed Ifugao huts, art galleries, and traditional crafts on a piney hillside.

name: Good Taste Restaurant
blurb: Baguio legend for huge, cheap servings — the buttered chicken is famous.

name: 50's Diner
blurb: Retro American diner with milkshakes, burgers, and vintage decor on Session Road.

name: Hill Station
blurb: Camp John Hay fine dining in a heritage house — try the bagnet pizza.

name: Café by the Ruins
blurb: Garden café in historic ruins serving Cordillera-inspired dishes and camote bread.

name: Picnic Grove
blurb: Pine-shaded picnic park with zipline rides and the classic Taal viewpoint.

name: Sky Ranch
blurb: Amusement park with the Sky Eye ferris wheel overlooking Taal Lake.

name: People's Park in the Sky
blurb: Unfinished palace turned hilltop viewpoint — the highest spot in Tagaytay.

name: Crosswinds
blurb: Swiss-inspired village with pine trees, cafés, and luxury stays.

name: Puzzle Mansion
blurb: Guinness-record jigsaw puzzle collection inside a cozy bed-and-breakfast.

name: Zipline at Picnic Grove
blurb: Soar over the ridge with Taal Volcano in your sightline.

name: Horseback Riding
blurb: Guided trail rides through pine forests near the ridge.

name: Museo Orlina
blurb: Glass-art museum with sculptures and a viewing deck over Taal.

name: Spa Day with a Taal View
blurb: Garden or in-room spa treatments with views over the lake.

name: Leslie's Restaurant
blurb: Home of the famous bulalo with a Taal view deck.

name: Mahogany Beef Market & Bulalohan
blurb: Tagaytay's legendary bulalo row — pick your beef at the market, they'll cook it.

name: Bag of Beans
blurb: Garden café famous for its blueberry cheesecake and Taal views.

name: Antonio's Restaurant
blurb: The Philippines' most awarded fine-dining restaurant in a garden estate.

name: Taal Volcano
blurb: The world's smallest active volcano — trek up for crater-lake views.

name: Anilao
blurb: The birthplace of Philippine diving — coral gardens and macro critters.

name: Laiya Beach
blurb: Long stretch of white sand in San Juan dotted with resorts.

name: Monte Maria Shrine
blurb: The towering Mother of All Asia statue overlooking Batangas Bay.

name: Mt. Gulugod Baboy
blurb: Beginner-friendly summit hike in Mabini with Batangas Bay views.

name: Scuba Diving in Anilao
blurb: Fun dives over coral slopes with turtles and frogfish — the macro capital.

name: Sombrero Island Snorkeling
blurb: Clear-water snorkeling around the hat-shaped islet off Tingloy.

name: Taal Volcano Trek
blurb: Boat across Taal Lake then hike to the crater rim viewpoint.

name: Batangas City Food Park
blurb: Late-night grills and live bands along the baywalk.

name: Café de Lipa
blurb: The home of Batangas barako — strong native coffee since the 1800s.

name: Liam's Lomi House
blurb: Batangas-style lomi — thick, eggy, and loaded, the province's soul food.

name: Gerry's Grill (SM Batangas)
blurb: Sizzling sisig and grilled seafood at this Filipino grill chain in SM City Batangas.

name: Empanada de Kaliskis Stalls
blurb: Taal's famous half-moon empanadas, fried fresh at the heritage town market.

name: Paoay Church
blurb: UNESCO-listed baroque church with massive buttresses — Ilocos' most iconic landmark.

name: Bangui Windmills
blurb: 20 giant turbines lined along Bangui Bay — the north's most photographed sight.

name: Sinking Bell Tower
blurb: Laoag's earthquake-sunk bell tower, a short walk from St. William's Cathedral.

name: Paoay Sand Dunes
blurb: Golden dunes near Laoag — the jump-off for 4x4 rides and sandboarding.

name: Kapurpurawan Rock Formation
blurb: Wind-sculpted white limestone cliffs on the Burgos coastline.

name: Sandboarding at Paoay Dunes
blurb: Ride a 4x4 to the dunes then sandboard down the slopes.

name: Laoag Heritage Walk
blurb: Stroll past ancestral houses and old churches in the historic center.

name: Pagudpud Beach Day
blurb: Powdery white sand and clear water at Saud Beach, the Boracay of the North.

name: Fort Ilocandia Casino
blurb: Gaming floors and live shows at Ilocos' landmark beachfront resort.

name: Herencia Café
blurb: Heritage-house café in Paoay serving Ilocano classics like pinakbet and bagnet.

name: Glory's Empanada
blurb: Batac's legendary empanada — crispy orange crust stuffed with papaya and egg.

name: Café Leona
blurb: Colonial-style café in a heritage house — try the tsokolate eh.

name: Saud Beach Seafood Grills
blurb: Beachfront grills serving fresh-caught fish and squid steps from the sand.

name: Big Lagoon
blurb: Emerald water between towering karsts — the star stop of Tour A.

name: Nacpan Beach
blurb: 4km of golden sand with twin-beach views from the hilltop.

name: Taraw Cliff
blurb: Sunrise canyoneering climb with panoramic views over Bacuit Bay.

name: Small Lagoon
blurb: Kayak through a narrow rock opening into a hidden turquoise cove.

name: Seven Commandos Beach
blurb: Palm-fringed Tour A beach with volleyball and fresh coconut stands.

name: Island Hopping Tour A
blurb: Big Lagoon, Small Lagoon, Secret Lagoon, and Shimizu Island in one day.

name: Scuba Diving Bacuit Bay
blurb: Dive WWII wrecks and coral walls with turtles and reef sharks.

name: Las Cabanas Sunset
blurb: Watch the sun melt into the sea from Las Cabanas Beach bars.

name: El Nido Nightlife
blurb: Beach bars and live music along Serena Street after dark.

name: Artcafé
blurb: Beachfront institution for wood-fired pizza and sunset dinners.

name: Trattoria Altrove
blurb: Beloved Italian spot — the garden setting and gnocchi are famous.

name: El Nido Talipapa Seafood
blurb: Pick live seafood at the market and have nearby eateries cook it your way.

name: Common Ground Café
blurb: All-day breakfast and strong coffee on El Nido's main strip.

name: Kayangan Lake
blurb: The famous viewpoint lake — swim in water so clear you can see 40m down.

name: Twin Lagoon
blurb: Swim under the rock arch between two lagoons — warm meets cool water.

name: Barracuda Lake
blurb: Surreal thermocline dive lake with jagged limestone walls.

name: Maquinit Hot Spring
blurb: Natural saltwater hot spring — perfect after a day of island hopping.

name: Mt. Tapyas
blurb: 700+ steps to the big cross with sunset views over Coron Bay.

name: WWII Wreck Diving
blurb: Dive sunken Japanese warships — among the world's best wreck sites.

name: Coron Ultimate Tour
blurb: Kayangan Lake, Twin Lagoon, and Siete Pecados in one epic day.

name: Siete Pecados Snorkeling
blurb: Seven islets with giant clams and clouds of colorful fish.

name: Coron Night Market
blurb: Grilled seafood and souvenirs at the town's evening market.

name: Lolo Nonoy's Food Station
blurb: Local favorite for grilled seafood and Filipino dishes near the market.

name: La Sirenetta
blurb: Waterfront seafood restaurant — great sunset views and fresh catch.

name: Bistro Coron
blurb: European-Filipino bistro on the main road — good steaks and pasta.

name: Kayangan Café
blurb: Rooftop café with bay views — good for breakfast before island tours.

name: Cloud 9
blurb: Siargao's iconic surf break with a boardwalk over the reef, famous for its perfect barreling waves.

name: Magpupungko Rock Pools
blurb: Natural tidal pools revealed at low tide, ideal for swimming and cliff jumping into crystal-clear water.

name: Sohoton Cove
blurb: A hidden cove on Bucas Grande with emerald lagoons, stingless jellyfish, and towering limestone cliffs.

name: Maasin River
blurb: A winding palm-fringed river famous for paddleboarding, rope swings, and the bent coconut tree photo spot.

name: Guyam Island
blurb: A tiny postcard-perfect islet with powdery white sand and palm trees, part of the tri-island hopping tour.

name: Sugba Lagoon
blurb: A stunning blue lagoon on Kawhagan Island with a diving platform, perfect for kayaking and swimming.

name: Surfing Lessons at Cloud 9
blurb: Learn to ride your first wave with a local instructor on the gentle beginner breaks near Cloud 9.

name: Tri-Island Hopping Tour
blurb: Boat-hop between Naked, Daku, and Guyam islands in one day, with snorkeling stops and beach picnics.

name: Stand-Up Paddleboarding
blurb: Glide along the calm Maasin River or lagoons at sunrise for a peaceful, scenic workout.

name: General Luna Nightlife
blurb: Beach bars and live music along Tourism Road keep the island buzzing after the sun goes down.

name: Shaka Siargao
blurb: Famous smoothie bowls, acai, and coffee in a tropical garden setting loved by surfers.

name: Fat Lips Surf Shack
blurb: Beachfront spot serving burgers, rice bowls, and cold drinks with live reggae vibes.

name: Kermit Siargao
blurb: Italian-Filipino fusion pizzas and pastas in a stylish surf-town setting near Cloud 9.

name: CEV: Ceviche & Kinilaw Shack
blurb: Fresh kinilaw and ceviche bowls made from the day's catch, right by the beach.

name: Philippine Eagle Center
blurb: Sanctuary protecting the majestic Philippine Eagle, with guided tours through lush forest enclosures.

name: People's Park
blurb: A beloved city park with waterfalls, ponds, sculptures, and a dancing fountain show at night.

name: Eden Nature Park
blurb: A mountain resort with gardens, sky rides, fishing village, and cool breezes above the city.

name: Mount Apo
blurb: The highest peak in the Philippines at 2,954m, a bucket-list climb for serious trekkers.

name: Davao Crocodile Park
blurb: Crocodile farm and wildlife park with feeding shows, tigers, and an exotic animal collection.

name: Samal Island
blurb: Island of white-sand beaches and resorts just a short ferry ride from the city waterfront.

name: Davao River White-Water Rafting
blurb: Thrilling rapids through tropical jungle just outside the city, with certified river guides.

name: Samal Island Beach Day
blurb: Ferry across the bay for a beach day, snorkeling, and resort pools with a city skyline backdrop.

name: Durian Tasting Tour
blurb: Brave the king of fruits at Magsaysay Park fruit stalls, where durian is a way of life.

name: Roxas Night Market
blurb: Famous night market for grilled tuna, street food stalls, and local snacks under the lights.

name: Penong's
blurb: Davao institution for chicken and pork barbecue served on banana leaves with unlimited rice.

name: Marina Tuna
blurb: Fresh tuna belly, sashimi, and kinilaw straight from the General Santos fishing grounds.

name: Claude's Le Cafe de Ville
blurb: Charming French-style cafe with pastries, cakes, and brewed coffee in the city center.

name: Lachi's
blurb: Beloved homestyle Filipino dishes in a cozy setting, from kare-kare to sizzling sisig.

name: White Island
blurb: A shifting white-sand bar off Mambajao with views of Mt. Hibok-Hibok, perfect for sunrise photos.

name: Sunken Cemetery
blurb: A giant cross marking a cemetery swallowed by a volcanic eruption, now a famous snorkeling site.

name: Katibawasan Falls
blurb: A 250-foot cascade plunging into a cool natural pool, surrounded by giant ferns and orchids.

name: Tuasan Falls
blurb: A rugged waterfall reached by a short trek through farmland, with a refreshing swimming pool.

name: Ardent Hot Spring
blurb: Naturally heated pools from Mt. Hibok-Hibok, wonderful for a soothing evening soak.

name: Mantigue Island
blurb: A marine sanctuary island with white beaches, giant clams, and excellent snorkeling.

name: Camiguin Island Loop Tour
blurb: Circle the whole island in a day by habal-habal or van, hitting waterfalls, springs, and viewpoints.

name: Snorkeling at Sunken Cemetery
blurb: Snorkel over coral gardens growing on the sunken tombstones, with giant clam sanctuaries nearby.

name: Hot Spring Evening Soak
blurb: Unwind in the warm mineral pools of Ardent Hot Spring after a day of island exploring.

name: Guiob Church Ruins Visit
blurb: Explore centuries-old church ruins left by the 1871 volcanic eruption, next to the old cemetery.

name: The Beehive
blurb: Cozy cafe serving hearty breakfasts, burgers, and fresh juices near the town center.

name: Luna Ristorante
blurb: Italian-inspired dishes and Filipino favorites in a garden restaurant in Mambajao.

name: Bahay Kubo Restaurant
blurb: Traditional Filipino dishes served in a nipa hut setting, with fresh grilled seafood.

name: Mapawa Nature Park
blurb: A riverside nature park with waterfalls, natural pools, and cliff-jumping spots in a scenic gorge.

name: Gaston Park & St. Augustine Cathedral
blurb: Historic plaza and cathedral at the heart of the city, perfect for an evening stroll.

name: Macahambus Hill Cave
blurb: A short trek leads to a cave gorge with a hanging bridge and WWII historical markers.

name: Seven Seas Waterpark
blurb: The country's largest pirate-themed waterpark with slides, a lazy river, and wave pools.

name: Divine Mercy Shrine
blurb: A 50-foot statue of the Divine Mercy overlooking Macajalar Bay, a popular pilgrimage site.

name: Cagayan River White-Water Rafting
blurb: The country's top rafting run, with beginner-friendly and extreme sections through jungle canyons.

name: Dahilayan Adventure Park Day Trip
blurb: Ride one of Asia's longest ziplines and cool pine-forest trails, an hour from the city.

name: Lifestyle District Nightlife
blurb: Bars, live bands, and late-night eats in the city's entertainment district.

name: Lechon Food Crawl
blurb: Taste the city's beloved roasted pork and local delicacies on a guided food crawl.

name: Kagay-on's
blurb: Classic Filipino buffet and grilled dishes in a spacious native-style dining hall.

name: Boy Zugba
blurb: Fun, colorful spot for affordable Filipino comfort food with a playful local vibe.

name: Missy Bon Bon
blurb: Beloved CDO bakeshop and cafe famous for cakes, pastries, and rich chocolate drinks.

name: Bigby's Cafe & Restaurant
blurb: A Mindanao-born chain serving hearty Filipino-Western plates loved by locals.

name: Great Santa Cruz Island
blurb: One of the world's rare pink-sand beaches, with coral gardens and mangrove lagoons.

name: Fort Pilar
blurb: A 17th-century Spanish fort housing a shrine and museum, the city's most iconic landmark.

name: Paseo del Mar
blurb: A scenic waterfront promenade perfect for sunset walks, street food, and sea views.

name: Merloquet Falls
blurb: A two-tiered waterfall with a natural infinity pool, hidden in the hills east of the city.

name: Yakan Weaving Village
blurb: Watch Yakan weavers create intricate traditional textiles and shop authentic handmade crafts.

name: Pink Beach Day Trip
blurb: Boat to Great Santa Cruz Island for pink sand, snorkeling, and a seafood lunch by the shore.

name: Yakan Weaving Workshop
blurb: Try your hand at the Yakan backstrap loom and learn the stories behind each pattern.

name: Merloquet Falls Trek
blurb: Trek through forest trails to the falls' infinity pool for a swim above the canopy.

name: Sunset at Paseo del Mar
blurb: Grab grilled snacks from the stalls and watch the sun sink over the Sulu Sea.

name: Alavar Seafood Restaurant
blurb: Zamboanga institution famous for curacha crabs in coconut milk and fresh seafood platters.

name: Dennis Coffee Garden
blurb: Garden cafe serving native coffee, fresh buko juice, and classic Filipino snacks.

name: Jimmy's Satti House
blurb: Local favorite for satti, Zamboanga's spicy Tausug-style grilled skewers with rice sauce.

name: Calle Crisologo
blurb: The famous half-kilometer cobblestone street lined with ancestral houses from the Spanish era. Best explored on foot or by calesa, especially in the early morning or at night when the street lamps glow.

name: Baluarte Mini Zoo
blurb: A mini zoo and animal sanctuary owned by the Singson family, with tigers, ostriches, and reptiles. Admission is free and the grounds include a butterfly garden and picnic areas.

name: Bantay Church Bell Tower
blurb: A historic hilltop bell tower in nearby Bantay that served as a watchtower during colonial times. Climb to the top for panoramic views of Vigan and the surrounding plains.

name: Syquia Mansion
blurb: The ancestral home of former president Elpidio Quirino, preserved as a museum with antique furniture and memorabilia. It gives a vivid look at ilustrado life in old Vigan.

name: Calesa Ride Around Heritage Village
blurb: Ride a horse-drawn calesa past the heritage houses, the cathedral, and the plazas with a kutsero who doubles as a guide. A signature Vigan experience, especially after sunset.

name: Dancing Fountain Show
blurb: A nightly fountain show at Plaza Salcedo with water, lights, and music telling the story of Ilocos. Shows usually run in the evening and draw big local crowds on weekends.

name: Cafe Leona
blurb: A beloved Vigan institution serving Ilocano classics like pinakbet, bagnet, and Vigan longganisa in a cozy ancestral house setting. A reliable first stop for heritage-town dining.

name: Vigan Empanadaan
blurb: A row of stalls near Plaza Burgos frying the famous Vigan empanada with orange rice-flour crust, longganisa, egg, and papaya. Pair it with sukang Iloko for the full experience.

name: Echo Valley and Hanging Coffins
blurb: A cliffside burial site where coffins of Sagada elders hang from limestone walls, reached by a short trail from the town center. A local guide is required and shares the stories behind this centuries-old tradition.

name: Sumaguing Cave
blurb: Sagada's most famous cave, with towering limestone formations, underground pools, and chambers reached by rappelling and wading. The standard 2-hour spelunking route needs a guide and basic fitness.

name: Kiltepan Peak Sunrise Viewpoint
blurb: A sunrise viewpoint famous for its sea of clouds rolling over the valley below. Arrive before dawn and dress warmly, since temperatures drop sharply at this elevation.

name: Bomod-ok Falls
blurb: A tall, powerful waterfall reached by a scenic trek through rice terraces from Banga-an village. Swimming is allowed in the catch basin on calm days.

name: Marlboro Hills Sunrise Trek
blurb: A pre-dawn trek to rolling hills with panoramic sunrise views over the Cordillera mountains. Local guides lead the hike and can arrange the connecting Blue Soil Hills side trip.

name: Sagada Yoghurt House
blurb: A cozy spot famous for its homemade yoghurt served with granola, honey, and local fruits. It also serves hearty mountain meals that hit the spot after a day of trekking.

name: Sagada Lemon Pie House
blurb: A Sagada institution baking its signature lemon pie along with other pastries and bread. A classic stop for dessert or pasalubong to bring home.

name: Ganduyan Museum
blurb: A small private museum of Igorot artifacts, weapons, and ritual objects collected over decades. It is a quick but meaningful stop to understand local culture before the treks.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces Viewpoint
blurb: The classic postcard viewpoint overlooking vast terraced slopes from the main road. Souvenir stalls and photo spots with traditional Ifugao costumes line the viewing area.

name: Batad Amphitheater Rice Terraces
blurb: A UNESCO-listed cluster of terraces shaped like a giant amphitheater, reached by a jeepney ride and a downhill trek from the saddle. It is widely considered the most beautiful terrace formation in the Cordilleras.

name: Tappiya Falls
blurb: A towering waterfall at the base of the Batad terraces, reached by a steep trek down from the village. The cold, powerful cascade is a rewarding finish after the terrace hike.

name: Bangaan Village
blurb: A traditional Ifugao village nestled in a bowl of rice terraces, also part of the UNESCO listing. A short trek from the road brings you into the village for homestays and cultural immersion.

name: Banaue Museum
blurb: A museum of Ifugao artifacts including bulul rice gods, weapons, and traditional clothing. It is a compact stop that deepens the terrace experience with cultural context.

name: Hapao Rice Terraces Trek
blurb: A longer trek through the Hungduan cluster of terraces, known for stone-walled paddies and hot springs along the route. Less crowded than Batad, with equally dramatic scenery.

name: People's Lodge Restaurant
blurb: A lodge restaurant serving Filipino and continental dishes with terrace views from its dining area. A convenient dinner spot for travelers staying in the town center.

name: Native Village Inn Restaurant
blurb: A native-style restaurant near the viewpoint road serving local Ifugao dishes and grilled meats. The nipa-hut dining setup adds to the highland atmosphere.

name: Sabang Beach
blurb: Baler's main surf beach with gentle rolling waves ideal for beginners and longboarders. Surf schools and board rentals line the shore, and the beach comes alive at sunrise with learners catching their first waves.

name: Diguisit Falls
blurb: A waterfall a short drive from town, reached by an easy walk through riverside scenery. A refreshing dip here is a classic add-on to the Diguisit rock formations trip.

name: Ditumabo Mother Falls
blurb: Known as the Mother Falls, this 140-foot cascade is reached by a scenic 30 to 45 minute trek from Barangay Ditumabo. It is one of Aurora's most photographed natural attractions.

name: Millennium Balete Tree
blurb: A centuries-old balete tree with massive roots you can climb on, located in the neighboring town of Maria Aurora. The 20 to 30 minute drive from Baler is a staple of the town's countryside tour.

name: Baler Church and Museo de Baler
blurb: A 17th-century church famous as the site of the Siege of Baler, where Spanish soldiers held out for nearly a year after the Philippine revolution. The adjacent museum tells the story of the last Spanish garrison in the country.

name: Dicasalarin Cove
blurb: A secluded cove with white sand and clear water, reached by a boat ride from Sabang or a trek over the hills. It is quieter than Sabang and popular for day-trip picnics.

name: Kusina Luntian
blurb: A garden restaurant serving Filipino comfort food with Baler touches, known for its relaxed open-air setting. A favorite dinner spot after a day of surfing.

name: Baler Surfer Grill
blurb: A beachfront grill serving seafood, sizzling dishes, and cold drinks steps from the surf. Live music nights make it a go-to hangout for the surf crowd.

name: Governor's Island
blurb: The island with the famous 123-step view deck overlooking the scattered islets of the national park. It also hosts a zipline and a narrow channel connecting it to Virgin Island at low tide.

name: Children's Island
blurb: A small island with a shallow lagoon popular for swimming and beginner snorkeling. Its calm waters make it a favorite family stop on the island-hopping route.

name: Marcos Island
blurb: An island known for Imelda Cave and a natural swimming pool enclosed by rock formations. It is one of the most scenic stops for photos and cliff jumping.

name: Quezon Island
blurb: A developed island with cottages, camping grounds, and snorkeling areas. Many tour packages use it as the lunch and swimming stop of the day.

name: Imelda Cave
blurb: A cave on Marcos Island where sunlight pours through an opening onto the water below, popular for cliff jumping and swimming. The drop into the water is a rite of passage for Hundred Islands visitors.

name: Hundred Islands Zipline
blurb: A 546-meter zipline flying from Governor's Island across the water, with views of the islets below. It is one of the most thrilling add-ons to the island-hopping tour.

name: Maxine by the Sea
blurb: A seafood restaurant near Lucap Wharf serving fresh catches, grilled squid, and Filipino classics. A natural lunch stop before or after the island-hopping tour.

name: Alaminos Town Eateries
blurb: A local eatery in Alaminos town known for Pangasinan dishes like pigar-pigar and bangus preparations. A good taste of the province beyond the wharf restaurants.

name: Cagsawa Ruins
blurb: The bell tower ruins of a church buried by Mayon's 1814 eruption, now the most iconic photo spot in Bicol. The park around it has ATV jump-off points and Mayon-facing viewpoints.

name: Mayon ATV Adventure
blurb: Ride an ATV across lava fields and riverbeds on Mayon's slopes, passing through landscapes shaped by past eruptions. Tour lengths range from short 45-minute runs to full-day black lava wall treks.

name: Lignon Hill Nature Park
blurb: A 156-meter hill in the city with a zipline and the best close-up sunrise views of Mayon Volcano. On clear mornings the volcano fills the entire horizon from the viewing deck.

name: Daraga Church
blurb: A baroque church perched on a hill in Daraga with Mayon Volcano perfectly framed behind it. One of the oldest stone churches in the Bicol region, built in the 1700s.

name: Sumlang Lake
blurb: A serene lake in Camalig with bamboo rafts and floating cottages, famous for its mirror-like reflections of Mayon. A quieter, greener alternative to the Cagsawa crowds.

name: Legazpi Boulevard
blurb: A 5-kilometer seaside boulevard with jogging paths, food stalls, and Mayon views across the water. The go-to sunset promenade for locals and visitors alike.

name: 1st Colonial Grill
blurb: The home of the famous sili ice cream, flavored with Bicol's fiery chili, plus pili desserts and Bicol dishes. A must-visit for adventurous eaters in Albay.

name: Waway's Restaurant
blurb: A local favorite serving Bicolano classics like Bicol express, laing, and pinangat with generous spice levels. Hearty servings at prices locals are happy to pay.

name: Lahos Island
blurb: A small island with white sand, clear water, and limestone cliffs, famous from Survivor seasons. One of the standard stops on the Caramoan island-hopping circuit.

name: Matukad Island
blurb: An island with a hidden lagoon enclosed by limestone karsts, reached by swimming through a narrow opening at low tide. One of Caramoan's most photographed natural formations.

name: Minalahos Island
blurb: A tiny island with a sandbar, a small chapel, and a giant cross on its limestone peak. The short climb rewards visitors with sweeping views of the surrounding islands.

name: Gota Beach
blurb: The jump-off beach for Caramoan island hopping, with boats lined up along its shore. The surrounding area also has coves and snorkeling spots worth exploring.

name: St. Michael the Archangel Church
blurb: The 17th-century parish church of Caramoan, dedicated to St. Michael the Archangel. Its red-brick facade is one of the oldest church structures in Camarines Sur.

name: Caramoan Island Hopping Tour
blurb: A full-day boat circuit visiting Lahos, Matukad, Minalahos, and other islets with stops for swimming and snorkeling. Boats are arranged at Paniman Beach through the tourism office.

name: Gota Village Resort Restaurant
blurb: The resort restaurant at Gota Beach serving Filipino dishes and fresh seafood with sea views. The most reliable full-service dining option near the island jump-off point.

name: Caramoan Town Eateries
blurb: Simple carinderias in the town proper serving Bicol dishes like laing and Bicol express at local prices. Stock up on meals here before heading to Paniman Beach.

name: Puerto Princesa Subterranean River
blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring an 8.2-kilometer navigable underground river through a limestone cave. Paddle boats glide past cathedral-like chambers filled with stalactites and bats.

name: Honda Bay Island Hopping
blurb: A group of islets including Cowrie, Starfish, and Luli Islands, known for white sand and excellent snorkeling. The standard island-hopping circuit is the city's most popular day tour after the Underground River.

name: Iwahig Firefly Watching
blurb: A nighttime paddle-boat tour where thousands of fireflies light up mangrove trees along the river. The star-filled sky over the water makes it one of Palawan's most magical evening experiences.

name: Baker's Hill
blurb: A park with butterfly gardens, colorful blooms, and a good view deck over the city. Its in-house bakeshop is famous for hopia and other pastries worth taking home.

name: Plaza Cuartel
blurb: A WWII memorial marking the site where American prisoners of war were killed in 1944. The small plaza and museum are a solemn reminder of Palawan's wartime history.

name: Immaculate Conception Cathedral
blurb: The city's main Catholic church with its distinctive blue facade, built in the late 1800s. It anchors the old town area near Plaza Cuartel and the baywalk.

name: Ka Lui Restaurant
blurb: A beloved seafood restaurant where diners eat barefoot on sand floors under nipa roofing. Famous for fresh grilled seafood and its charming, rustic atmosphere.

name: Badjao Seafront Restaurant
blurb: A seafront restaurant on stilts over the water, perfect for sunset dinners of Filipino and seafood dishes. Live acoustic music adds to the bayfront atmosphere.

name: Urbiztondo Beach
blurb: The main surf beach of La Union with consistent beach-break waves suitable for beginners and intermediates. Surf schools line the shore, and the sunset sessions here are legendary.

name: El Union Coffee
blurb: A famous surf-town cafe credited with kickstarting La Union's coffee culture, serving slow-bar coffee and brunch. Expect lines on weekends, but the people-watching is worth it.

name: Flotsam and Jetsam
blurb: A beachfront food park with container stalls, live DJs, and fire dancers, and one of the birthplaces of Elyu's party scene. The place to be after the sun goes down on weekends.

name: Tangadan Falls
blurb: A multi-tiered waterfall in nearby San Gabriel, reached by a trek through rice fields and forest trails. The deep natural pools are perfect for cliff jumping and swimming.

name: Surf Lessons at Urbiztondo
blurb: Take a lesson from one of the many accredited surf schools along Urbiztondo Beach. Instructors provide boards and an hour of coaching, with most beginners standing up by the end.

name: Tagpuan
blurb: A go-to spot for Mexican-Filipino fusion, famous for its tacos and nachos served steps from the sand. A staple of the Urbiztondo food crawl.

name: Urbiztondo Point View Deck
blurb: A cliffside viewpoint and small park overlooking the surf break, popular for sunrise and sunset photos. A short walk from the main beach strip.

name: Donsol Whale Shark Interaction
blurb: The main whale shark interaction site, where spotters locate butanding and boats bring swimmers to snorkel beside them. Strict rules keep the experience safe for both visitors and the gentle giants.

name: Swimming with Whale Sharks
blurb: Snorkel or free-dive beside whale sharks under the guidance of trained Butanding Interaction Officers. November to June offers the best chances of sightings.

name: Ogod River Firefly Watching
blurb: A peaceful night cruise on the Ogod River where fireflies cluster in the riverside trees. The calm water and dark skies make it a romantic end to a whale shark day.

name: Manta Bowl Dive Site
blurb: A world-class dive site off nearby Ticao Island known for manta ray encounters and cleaning stations. Advanced divers visit from Donsol for day trips during the season.

name: Donsol Tourism Center
blurb: The registration and briefing center for all whale shark interactions, with exhibits about butanding conservation. Every tour starts here with an orientation from the tourism office.

name: Vitton Beach Resort Restaurant
blurb: A beachfront resort restaurant serving Bicol dishes and fresh seafood with views of Donsol Bay. A convenient meal stop after the morning whale shark tour.

name: Amor Farm Beach Resort Restaurant
blurb: A beach resort restaurant known for Filipino comfort food and grilled seafood in a garden setting. A relaxing dinner spot for divers and whale shark watchers.

name: Alubihod Beach
blurb: A quiet cove in Nueva Valencia with white sand, calm water, and island views. It is the island's most developed beach area, lined with small resorts.

name: Guisi Lighthouse
blurb: An 18th-century Spanish-era lighthouse standing on a cliff in Barangay Guisi. The short climb rewards visitors with wide views of the sea and the horizon.

name: Balaan Bukid Shrine
blurb: A hilltop shrine in Buenavista marked by a large white cross visible from Iloilo. The climb passes the Stations of the Cross and ends with a panoramic view of the Iloilo Strait.

name: Natago Beach Island Hopping
blurb: Pump boats from Alubihod visit nearby islets such as Natago Beach and Ave Maria Islet. Expect sandbars, snorkeling spots, and clear shallow water.

name: Mango Plantation Tour
blurb: Tour the mango orchards that made Guimaras famous and taste fresh carabao mangoes in season. Some farms let visitors pick fruit or buy by the kilo.

name: Pitstop Restaurant
blurb: A well-known stop in Buenavista famous for its mango pizza and mango-based dishes. It is the classic lunch break on any Guimaras road trip.

name: Monad Shoal
blurb: A submerged plateau where thresher sharks visit cleaning stations at sunrise. Dawn dives here are the island's signature experience for certified divers.

name: Bounty Beach
blurb: The island's main white-sand beach, lined with resorts, dive shops, and bars. It faces west, so sunsets here are a nightly event.

name: Gato Island
blurb: A small rocky islet and marine reserve known for whitetip sharks, sea snakes, and a swim-through tunnel. It is a favorite second dive after Monad Shoal.

name: Thresher Shark Dawn Dive
blurb: Join a 5 a.m. dive briefing and descend to Monad Shoal as the thresher sharks arrive. Open Water certification and good buoyancy control are required.

name: Kalanggaman Sandbar Day Trip
blurb: Speedboats run day trips to the famous Kalanggaman sandbar, about an hour away. Trips usually include lunch, snorkeling stops, and beach time.

name: Ging-Ging's Restaurant
blurb: A long-running beachfront spot serving Filipino dishes, fresh seafood, and breakfast sets. It is a favorite among divers refueling between dives.

name: Kalanggaman Sandbar
blurb: The island's famous white sandbar extends hundreds of meters into clear blue water. Walk its full length at low tide for the classic panoramic photos.

name: Kalanggaman Reef
blurb: Coral gardens and reef slopes surround the island with decent visibility on calm days. Expect small reef fish, corals, and occasional sea turtles.

name: Island Kayaking
blurb: Rent a kayak and paddle around the island or out toward the sandbar tip. The water is usually calmest in the morning.

name: Beach Volleyball
blurb: Join pickup beach volleyball games on the main beach, a favorite pastime of overnight campers. Equipment is sometimes available from the tourism staff.

name: Palompon Public Market
blurb: Stock up on grilled food, rice meals, and snacks at Palompon Public Market before boarding the boat. Most visitors bring all their food since the island has no restaurants.

name: Palompon Port Carinderias
blurb: Small carinderias near Palompon Port serve hot Filipino meals to day-trippers before or after the crossing. A practical breakfast stop before the early boat.

name: The Ruins
blurb: The skeletal remains of a grand 1900s sugar baron mansion in Talisay, lit beautifully at night. It is the most photographed landmark in Negros.

name: San Sebastian Cathedral
blurb: A 19th-century stone church in the city center and the seat of the Bacolod diocese. Its coral-stone facade is a quiet contrast to the busy plaza outside.

name: Negros Museum
blurb: A museum of Negrense history, art, and the sugar industry housed in a former agricultural building. Good for a quick culture stop between food trips.

name: MassKara Festival
blurb: Every October, dancers in colorful smiling masks parade through the streets for MassKara. Book hotels early, since the city fills up for the festival week.

name: Mambukal Resort Day Trip
blurb: Mambukal Resort in Murcia offers hot sulfur springs, waterfalls, and forest trails about an hour from the city. It is the classic Bacolod weekend escape.

name: Manokan Country
blurb: A row of open-air stalls grilling chicken inasal over charcoal near SM City Bacolod. This is the pilgrimage site for the city's signature dish.

name: Aida's Chicken
blurb: Aida's is one of the original inasal houses, famous for its paa and pecho with chicken oil rice. Expect a line at peak meal times.

name: Calea Pastries
blurb: Calea is beloved for its cakes, especially the chocolate and mango variants, at prices far below Manila cafes. Boxes of cake are a standard pasalubong.

name: Apo Island Marine Sanctuary
blurb: The protected reef in front of the village where turtles, corals, and schools of fish thrive. A guide and sanctuary fee are required to snorkel here.

name: Chapel Point
blurb: A coral-covered point on the island's south side with turtles, bumphead parrotfish, and occasional reef sharks. A favorite for both snorkelers and divers.

name: Lighthouse Viewpoint
blurb: A short hike up to the old lighthouse offers a full view of the island and the sea toward Negros. Best visited late in the afternoon for softer light.

name: Sea Turtle Snorkeling
blurb: Float over the sanctuary reef as green sea turtles surface for air around you. Guides know the cleaning spots where turtles linger longest.

name: Apo Island Scuba Diving
blurb: Dive sites like Coconut Point and Rock Point West offer drift dives along coral walls. Currents can be strong, so they suit experienced divers.

name: Liberty's Lodge Restaurant
blurb: Liberty's Lodge runs a simple restaurant serving Filipino meals and fresh seafood to guests and walk-ins. Meals are hearty after a morning in the water.

name: Pearl Farm Beach Resort
blurb: The iconic overwater-cottage resort on a private islet off Samal. Day tour guests can use the pools, beach, and restaurants with a prior booking.

name: Monfort Bat Sanctuary
blurb: Home to around two million fruit bats, recognized by Guinness as the largest colony of its kind. Guided walks pass viewing decks at dusk when the bats stream out.

name: Vanishing Island
blurb: A sandbar off Barangay Tambo that appears and disappears with the tide. Boats from the mainland coast make the short crossing at low tide.

name: Coral Garden Snorkeling
blurb: Snorkel the Coral Garden marine sanctuary with its giant clams and coral formations. Local guides provide gear and know the calmest entry points.

name: Samal Island Hopping Tour
blurb: Boat tours link Kaputian Beach, the Vanishing Island, and snorkeling stops in one trip. Most tours leave in the morning and return by mid-afternoon.

name: Kaputian Seafood Grills
blurb: Grill restaurants along the Kaputian coast serve fresh catch, kinilaw, and grilled squid. Pick your fish from the display and have it cooked to order.

name: Dahican Beach
blurb: A 7-kilometer crescent of white sand facing the Pacific, famous for skimboarding and surfing. The beach stays relatively uncrowded outside event season.

name: Sleeping Dinosaur Viewpoint
blurb: A rock formation on Pujada Bay that looks like a dinosaur lying in the water. The viewpoint above it offers the classic photo of the bay.

name: Subangan Museum
blurb: A natural history museum in Mati city housing the skeleton of a sperm whale found in the area. Exhibits cover Davao Oriental's marine and forest life.

name: Dahican Skimboarding
blurb: Rent a skimboard or take a lesson on Dahican's shore break, where the sport took root in the Philippines. Amihan sa Dahican runs lessons and hosts competitions.

name: Turtle Hatchling Release
blurb: Watch hatchling releases at Dahican during nesting season, usually with guidance from local conservation groups. Releases often happen at sunset.

name: Dahican Seafood Grills
blurb: Beachfront grills along Dahican serve fresh tuna, squid, and kinilaw at local prices. Many resorts also cook the day's catch for guests.

name: Mati Baywalk Food Stalls
blurb: Evening food stalls at Mati Baywalk offer barbecue, street food, and shakes with a view of Pujada Bay. A favorite hangout for locals after sunset.

name: Seven Falls
blurb: A series of seven waterfalls in the rainforest, with the first two reachable by a short trek. Hikong Bente, the tallest, is crossed by the famous zipline.

name: Punta Isla
blurb: Punta Isla sits on a small island in the lake with floating cottages, a restaurant, and gardens. It is the classic lunch stop for its tilapia dishes.

name: T'boli Museum
blurb: A small museum of T'boli artifacts, brass work, and musical instruments in the town center. It gives context to the weaving and culture seen around the lake.

name: Seven Falls Zipline
blurb: Ride one of the highest ziplines in Southeast Asia over Hikong Bente falls at 180 meters up. The tandem ride gives a full aerial view of the falls and forest.

name: Sunrise Lake Cruise
blurb: Cruise the lake at sunrise past lotus flowers, fish cages, and stilt houses. Pump boats leave from the Punta Isla area and nearby docks.

name: Lakeside Tilapia Restaurants
blurb: Lakeside restaurants serve the town's famous tilapia, raised in the lake's fish cages, grilled or cooked in coconut milk. Punta Isla's restaurant is the best known.

name: Tinuy-an Falls
blurb: A 95-meter-wide, multi-tiered waterfall cascading into a turquoise basin. Bamboo rafts take visitors right under the curtain of water for the full experience.

name: Hinatuan Enchanted River
blurb: The famous deep-blue river in nearby Hinatuan where fish feeding happens at noon daily. Swimming is limited to a designated area to protect the spring.

name: Bislig Baywalk
blurb: Bislig Baywalk is an evening promenade along the coast with food stalls and sea views. Locals gather here at sunset for snacks and the ocean breeze.

name: Tinuy-an Bamboo Raft Ride
blurb: Ride a bamboo raft to the base of Tinuy-an Falls and feel the waterfall's spray up close. Life vests are provided and the ride takes about 15 minutes.

name: Enchanted River Swim
blurb: Swim in the designated area of the Enchanted River's impossibly clear blue water. The daily fish feeding at noon is the highlight to time your visit around.

name: Tinuy-an Jump-off Carinderias
blurb: Carinderias near the Tinuy-an Falls jump-off serve rice meals and grilled seafood to day-trippers. Bislig city's eateries offer the same at local prices.

name: Baywalk Evening Food Stalls
blurb: Evening stalls at Bislig Baywalk sell barbecue, grilled tuna, and refreshments by the sea. It doubles as dinner and sunset viewing.

name: Magellan's Cross
blurb: Historic wooden cross planted by Spanish explorers in 1521.

name: Basilica Minore del Santo Nino
blurb: The country's oldest Catholic church, home to the revered Santo Nino statue.

name: Tops Lookout
blurb: Hilltop viewpoint in Busay with sweeping views of Cebu City, Mactan, and the sea.

name: Cebu Taoist Temple
blurb: Colorful Taoist temple in Beverly Hills with dragon motifs and city views.

name: Kawasan Falls
blurb: Famous turquoise waterfalls in Badian — swim, raft, or start canyoneering here.

name: Whale Shark Watching (Oslob)
blurb: Snorkel beside gentle whale sharks with trained local spotters.

name: Canyoneering at Kawasan
blurb: Cliff jumps, natural slides, and river trekking down to Kawasan Falls.

name: Mactan Island Hopping
blurb: Boat tour to Hilutungan and Caohagan islets for snorkeling and seafood lunch.

name: Mango Square Nightlife
blurb: Cebu's classic nightlife strip with bars, clubs, and late-night eats.

name: Larsian BBQ
blurb: Legendary open-air barbecue row near Fuente — grilled pork, chicken, and isaw.

name: Sutukil Seafood (Mactan Newtown)
blurb: Pick fresh seafood from the market and have it cooked sugba, tuwa, or kilaw.

name: Lantaw Native Restaurant
blurb: Filipino dishes with sea views at SRP — great for sunset dinners.

name: Abaca Baking Company
blurb: Cebu's beloved artisan bakery and cafe — croissants, cakes, and good coffee.

name: Chocolate Hills
blurb: Over a thousand cone-shaped hills that turn chocolate-brown in the dry season.

name: Alona Beach
blurb: Panglao's famous white-sand beach lined with dive shops, bars, and restaurants.

name: Philippine Tarsier Sanctuary
blurb: See tiny wide-eyed tarsiers in a protected forest habitat in Corella.

name: Baclayon Church
blurb: One of the oldest stone churches in the Philippines, dating back to 1596.

name: Balicasag Island
blurb: Small island with sea turtles and coral walls — a top Visayas dive site.

name: Diving in Panglao
blurb: Dive coral gardens and spot sea turtles at Balicasag and Pamilacan.

name: Loboc River Cruise
blurb: Floating restaurant cruise with a buffet lunch and live acoustic music.

name: Firefly Watching (Abatan River)
blurb: Evening paddle boat tour to see thousands of fireflies light up the mangroves.

name: ATV Ride at Chocolate Hills
blurb: Muddy ATV adventure around the foothills of the Chocolate Hills.

name: Gerarda's Restaurant
blurb: Beloved Boholano spot for Filipino comfort food near Alona Beach.

name: The Buzz Cafe
blurb: Beachfront cafe at Bellevue known for all-day breakfast and good coffee.

name: Shaka Bohol
blurb: Surfer-style cafe with smoothie bowls and strong espresso near the beach.

name: Bohol Bee Farm
blurb: Organic garden restaurant in Dao famous for flower salads and ube ice cream.

name: White Beach Station 2
blurb: The heart of Boracay — 4 km of powdery white sand and calm turquoise water.

name: Puka Shell Beach
blurb: Quieter northern beach famous for puka shells and dramatic sunsets.

name: Mount Luho View Deck
blurb: The island's highest point with 360-degree views of the whole island.

name: Ariel's Point
blurb: Cliff-jumping spot on the southern tip with 5 diving platforms up to 15m.

name: Willy's Rock
blurb: Iconic volcanic rock with a grotto shrine — Boracay's most photographed spot.

name: Parasailing
blurb: Soar above White Beach for unbeatable views of the island.

name: Island Hopping Tour
blurb: Visit Puka Beach, snorkel spots, and Crystal Cove with a seafood lunch.

name: Sunset Paraw Sailing
blurb: Glide along White Beach on a traditional paraw sailboat at golden hour.

name: OM Bar
blurb: Beachfront club with fire dancers and DJs — a Boracay nightlife staple.

name: Cha Cha's Beach Cafe
blurb: Beachfront Filipino-Spanish dishes with your toes in the sand.

name: Jonah's Fruit Shake
blurb: Legendary fruit shakes — mango, banana-choco, and avocado are must-tries.

name: D'Talipapa (Paluto)
blurb: Buy fresh seafood at the wet market and have stalls cook it your way.

name: The Sunny Side Cafe
blurb: Trendy all-day breakfast spot famous for ube pancakes and good coffee.

name: Molo Church
blurb: Gothic church known as the 'feminist church' for its all-female saints.

name: Iloilo River Esplanade
blurb: Long riverside promenade perfect for jogging, biking, and sunset walks.

name: Gigantes Islands
blurb: Offshore islands in Carles with lagoons, sandbars, and famous scallops.

name: Miagao Church
blurb: UNESCO-listed baroque church with a stunning fortress-like facade.

name: Museo Iloilo
blurb: Provincial museum with Panay artifacts, fossils, and contemporary art.

name: Bike the Esplanade
blurb: Rent a bike and ride the riverside esplanade at golden hour.

name: Gigantes Island Hopping
blurb: Boat tour to Cabugao Gamay, Antonia Beach, and a scallop lunch.

name: Garin Farm
blurb: Pilgrimage park in San Joaquin with a hilltop cross and panoramic views.

name: Smallville Nightlife
blurb: Iloilo's main nightlife complex — bars, clubs, and restaurants in one strip.

name: Netong's La Paz Batchoy
blurb: Home of the original La Paz Batchoy — rich pork noodle soup.

name: Roberto's Siopao
blurb: Famous for the Queen Siopao — a giant steamed bun stuffed with fillings.

name: Breakthrough Restaurant
blurb: Seaside seafood institution in Villa — buttered shrimp and grilled fish.

name: Coffeebreak
blurb: Homegrown Iloilo coffee chain — good brews and all-day breakfast.

name: Cambugahay Falls
blurb: Three-tiered falls in Lazi — swim, swing, and jump from the platforms.

name: Salagdoong Beach
blurb: Cliff-lined beach in Maria with famous jumping platforms into clear water.

name: Century-Old Balete Tree
blurb: Massive 400-year-old balete tree with a fish spa in its spring pool.

name: Paliton Beach
blurb: 'Little Boracay' in San Juan — fine white sand and shallow calm water.

name: Lazi Church
blurb: Historic coral-stone church and Asia's largest old convent beside it.

name: Cliff Jumping at Salagdoong
blurb: Leap from 7m or 10m platforms into deep turquoise water.

name: Fish Spa at Balete Tree
blurb: Dip your feet in the spring pool and let the doctor fish nibble away.

name: Snorkeling at Tubod Marine Sanctuary
blurb: Protected reef in San Juan with corals, giant clams, and sea turtles.

name: Bolo-Bolo Healing Ritual
blurb: Experience Siquijor's traditional faith-healing with local mananambal.

name: Baha Bar
blurb: Beach bar and grill in San Juan — live music, cocktails, and sunsets.

name: Monkey Business
blurb: Laid-back spot for Filipino-Western food and legendary banana pancakes.

name: Makarios Restaurant
blurb: Cozy Filipino restaurant known for generous portions and home cooking.

name: Coco Grove Restaurant
blurb: Seafood and Filipino classics inside Coco Grove Beach Resort.

name: Rizal Boulevard
blurb: Scenic seaside promenade — the city's living room for sunsets and street food.

name: Silliman University
blurb: Historic campus founded in 1901 with acacia-lined walks and museums.

name: Apo Island
blurb: World-famous marine reserve — swim with sea turtles over coral gardens.

name: Tierra Alta Lighthouse
blurb: Greek-inspired lighthouse in Valencia with sweeping bay views.

name: Pulangbato Falls
blurb: Red-rock waterfall in Valencia — swim in the cool natural pools.

name: Dive with Turtles at Apo Island
blurb: Snorkel or dive with resident sea turtles in a protected marine sanctuary.

name: Red Rock Hot Spring
blurb: Soak in warm sulfur pools in the Valencia highlands.

name: Buglasan Festival
blurb: Negros Oriental's biggest festival every October — street dancing and shows.

name: Sunset Stroll on the Boulevard
blurb: Walk Rizal Boulevard at golden hour and grab tempura from street carts.

name: Without Name (A Italian Table)
blurb: Beloved Italian restaurant on the boulevard — handmade pasta and pizza.

name: Kri
blurb: Upscale Filipino restaurant on the boulevard with creative local dishes.

name: Sans Rival Cakes & Pastries
blurb: Dumaguete institution famous for silvanas, sans rival, and pastries.

name: Jo's Chicken Inato
blurb: Local favorite for grilled chicken inato with unlimited rice options.
